l01: I watch this camera every night. And every night he stands a little closer.
l02: The Horizon needed a night guard. Three to six. Triple pay. I didn't ask why.
l03: The other guard was already in his jacket. Keys and a sheet of paper ready in his hand.
l04: And he practically ran out into the street.
l05: One. At three a.m. the lights on the seventh floor will come on. Do not go up.
l06: Two. If the elevator arrives on its own, do not get in.
l07: Three. After midnight, let no one in. Not even your own.
l08: Four. Do not turn on camera thirteen.
l09: And at the bottom someone had added in pen: rule three is a lie. Let her in. Signed — M.
l10: Above the desk hung the last guard's pass. "Mikhailov." A month ago he went on his rounds and never came back.
l11: I stayed. The seventh floor was lit, the corridor empty. And then I realized I couldn't hear the rain. At all.
l12: Then the elevator chimed. Nobody had called it. The doors opened and stayed open. I started counting.
l13: I never touched camera thirteen. It turned on by itself. The button was dead — all that was left was the cord.
l14: Half past three. Katya was standing behind the glass. My sister. Who lives three hundred kilometers away.
l15: Tyoma. Only she ever called me that. When we were kids.
l16: I checked the entrance camera. Where she stood, there was nothing but static.
l17: I reached for the key. On the other side, she pressed her palm to the glass. Right against mine.
ch_guard: Here, take these. Read the sheet. And don't get clever — do exactly what it says.
ch_katya: Tyoma… Open up. Please. I'm freezing.
ch_whisper: Open up… Open up for me.
intro_2: Mom needed treatment. When they pay triple, you don't ask questions.

cam13_0: Fifty-nine. Sixty. The doors closed. The elevator went up. To where there are no floors.

open_2: — It's okay, it's okay. You're inside. You're safe now.

open_9: Seventh-floor camera. At the end of the corridor — a yellow raincoat. She slowly turned around.
open_10: It wasn't her face. And it was smiling into the camera.
open_11: Wet ink. Mikhalych never wrote that note. It was written tonight. For me.
open_12: It forged his handwriting. And I opened the door for it myself.
open_13: The elevator hummed. Seven. Six. Five. It was coming down.

booth_1: Ding. The elevator doors. Footsteps. Bare, wet. Closer.

sister_6: — Why aren't you saying anything? Come in. I've already opened the door.

stay_6: — Hello… Tyoma? Do you know what time it is?

dawn_4: — Thank you, son. I haven't seen the sky in a month.
